- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 periods ahead.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong bearish momentum, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply a downward bias correction of 1–4% depending on sentiment severity.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 85% of historical mean, reduce forecast; if below 75%, increase forecast — especially when sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish; apply a 1–3% downward adjustment for first 5 days.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to misalign with sentiment shifts; align forecast slope with sentiment direction change.
